record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.original_question: How can cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) support communication with backscattering or energy-neutral devices, including integration with simultaneous transmission and reception from different distributed panels, without breaking the time-division-duplex flow or compromising coherent cell-free operation?

evidence.quote: In addition to the key questions addressed in this paper, there are still many interesting research questions requiring future comprehensive studies, such as 1) At what level of densification is CF-MMIMO truly beneficial? When is it not really needed?; 2) How to handle high mobility in UDNs with CF-MMIMO?; 3) CF-MMIMO for communication with backscattering devices
A fifth is the integration of service of energy-neutral devices that communicate via backscattering.

CF-MMIMO naturally offers the infrastructure for that, permitting simultaneous transmission and reception from different panels in a bistatic setup; however, these activities break the TDD flow and must be carefully integrated into the workings of the system.

artifact.category_tag: Cell-free massive MIMO with backscatter devices
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) wireless system consisting of a large number L of geographically distributed access points (APs), each equipped with multiple antenna panels, jointly serving K single-antenna user equipments (UEs) over the same time-frequency resources. The APs are connected via a fronthaul to one or more central processing units that perform coherent joint signal processing (joint precoding on the downlink and joint combining on the uplink). The system operates in time-division-duplex (TDD) mode: each coherence block of length τ_c channel uses is partitioned into an uplink pilot phase of length τ_p, an uplink data phase of length τ_u, and a downlink data phase of length τ_d, with τ_p + τ_u + τ_d = τ_c. Channel state information is acquired at the APs via uplink pilots and used coherently in both transmission directions by exploiting channel reciprocity.

Suppose that, in addition to the K active UEs, the system must also serve a set of M energy-neutral backscatter devices. Each backscatter device m has no active radio-frequency source: it modulates information by reflecting an incident carrier signal with a complex reflection coefficient Γ_m(t) ∈ ℂ, |Γ_m(t)| ≤ 1, drawn from a finite signaling constellation. Communication with such a device is therefore inherently bistatic: at any given instant, a subset of the APs (or panels) must transmit an illuminating carrier waveform toward the device while a (possibly disjoint) subset must simultaneously receive and decode the backscattered signal. This simultaneous transmit/receive operation across distributed panels does not fit the standard TDD partitioning above.

Formulate and analyze a system-level framework that achieves all of the following simultaneously:

(a) A precise definition of frame structure, pilot allocation, and scheduling rules that allow a subset of APs/panels to transmit illumination signals to backscatter devices while another subset coherently receives the backscattered signal, without destroying the coherent uplink/downlink TDD operation for the K active UEs.

(b) Channel estimation procedures for the composite forward (AP→device) and backward (device→AP) backscatter channels, including handling of the direct AP-to-AP self-interference and clutter induced by simultaneous transmission and reception.

(c) Joint precoding for illumination and joint combining for backscatter reception, designed coherently across distributed APs, together with downlink precoding and uplink combining for the active UEs, such that interference between the two services is controlled.

(d) An achievable-rate or detection-performance characterization for the backscatter devices and an achievable spectral-efficiency characterization for the active UEs under the proposed framework, identifying the fundamental trade-offs between the resources (time, frequency, spatial degrees of freedom, fronthaul) allocated to backscatter service versus conventional CF-MMIMO service.

Determine whether such a framework exists and, if so, exhibit one and quantify the resulting trade-offs.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a future-research direction in the area of cell-free massive MIMO. Existing literature has begun to study CF-MMIMO with backscatter/ambient backscatter and bistatic sensing, but a complete framework that handles joint TDD scheduling, coherent operation, and energy-neutral device integration without disrupting the cell-free pilot/data structure has not been established as of 2026. The problem is treated as an open research direction.
